speaker: Doctor
text: I have noted your report of progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. To begin my evaluation, please describe exactly when these symptoms started and if you have noticed any redness, warmth, or changes in the skin over the affected finger.

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That mechanism of injury—specifically being pulled by a jersey—suggests an avulsion injury. Have you noticed any visible deformity, a "tear" in the skin, or an inability to make a fist with your right hand?

REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray right hand (AP and lateral views) to evaluate for ring avulsion fracture or tendon rupture.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (extensor tendon rupture of the distal phalanx).

The inability to actively flex the distal interphalangeal joint, combined with the finger resting in extension and the history of a jersey pulling away, confirms a rupture of the extensor tendon. This injury typically requires splinting; if there is significant subungual hematoma or bone avulsion visible on the X-ray I requested, surgical consultation may be considered.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
